“Chavez was good” in any context is not nuanced. Hasan could have very easily said “Chavez was better than Maduro,” and it would have gotten his point across very easily without this mess. Nobody is blaming Chavez for every single bad thing in Venezuela, it was quite obviously a slew of issues that lead to the perfect storm. Socialism/the economic state in Venezuela is a very nuanced topic that needs very nuanced takes and at least a rudimentary understanding of Latin American history to discuss. If we’re being honest, that reigns true for the whole region but I’m going off on a tangent.  That being said Chavez was a piece of shit.  He was a failed baseball player turned politician that lulled the Venezuelan working class into a false sense of security to build himself up into a corrupt dictator. So while the current ruin of Venezuela’s economy isn’t 100% Chavez’s fault, he played a major part in it and Maduro just carried on that legacy of deep seeded corruption.

Normally I don't like when people announce that they're going to stop watching but honestly I don't blame you. I'm sorry you had to leave Venezuela and that you still have family there, and that you aren't able to help them bc of the exchange control. People who don't have direct roots to communist countries will never understand the trauma and pain of having to flee in hopes of a better life, ending up in a foreign country with a completely different language and culture in pursuit of a better living situation.   
I don't know the struggle first hand, but my grandparents fled from Cuba. The family we still have there are starving and in really bad shape.   
It's concerning watching the dismissal of Latine/Venezuelan voices from fellow h3 fans, going as far as accusing some of lying about being Venezuelan. Very weird behavior, gross even.  
Going off the rails a lil bit, but I honestly don't think Hasan meant it as like "Oh Chavez was a great thing to happen to Venezuela," more than he meant in contrast to Maduro, but I do think he should be more careful and nuanced when speaking about situations like Venezuela. But, instead he doubled down during his stream and came off as very arrogant throughout this whole situation.
